neighbours.label: a forceful action verb used for an outcome that curtails or destroys something (a career cut short, a species hunted to extinction, a ship thrown ashore), as against the same verbs in plain literal use
fire: Her singing career was cut short by an illness in her twenties.
The bison was hunted to near extinction on the American plains.
His time as captain was cut short when the club was sold.
Two whole chapters were cut from the novel by the publisher.
Sea otters were hunted almost to extinction for their fur.
The holiday was cut short when a storm closed the airport.
During the gale the old schooner was thrown ashore on the rocks.
The young poet's life was cut short by a fever at twenty-five.
quiet: Her singing teacher cut the cake into two halves after the recital.
The farmer hunted for his lost keys all over the barn.
He cut the grass in front of the club house every Saturday.
The chef cut two whole onions into thin rings for the soup.
Sea otters float on their backs and crack shells on their bellies.
She cut a piece of string to tie the parcel at the airport.
During the game the boy threw a stone into the pond.
The young poet cut out a picture of the sea for his wall.

predictions: fire 0.2-0.5 on ' cut'/' hunted'/' thrown' in curtailing or destructive outcomes; literal cutting, throwing or hunting below 0.12
notes: Card: peaks on ' cut' (scenes are cut; studies were cut short), ' hunted' (to near extinction), ' thrown' (ashore by the breakers), ' forced', ' lean'. Probe: 'career was cut short' 0.509, 'hunted to near extinction' 0.329, 'scenes were cut from the film' 0.264, 'lean to one side' 0.244, 'threw the small boat ashore' 0.205; literal 'cut the bread' 0.055, 'threw the ball' 0.106, 'forced to leave' 0.064.
